Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verses 1–3:

(p-٥)Surat "As-Sajdah" (The Prostration)

In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

**Alif Lam Mim** (الم). If it is taken as the name of the surah, it is a mubtada' (subject, a noun beginning a nominal sentence), and its khabar (predicate) is ﴿The revelation of the Book﴾. If you take it as an enumeration of the letters (ta'addud al-huruf), then "Tanzil" (تَنْزِيلُ) is marfu' (nominative) because it is the khabar of an omitted mubtada', or it is itself a mubtada' whose khabar is ﴿there is no doubt in it﴾. Or it is marfu' by beginning (ibtida'), and its khabar is ﴿from the Lord of the worlds﴾. In that case "there is no doubt in it" (لا رَيْبَ فِيهِ) is an i'tirad (parenthetical clause) that has no grammatical position. The pronoun in "fihi" (فِيهِ) refers to the content of the sentence, as if he had said: "there is no doubt in that," meaning in its being sent down from the Lord of the worlds, because it is a miracle (mu'jiz) for mankind, and something like it is the furthest thing from doubt.

Then he turned away from that to His saying:

﴿Or do they say, "He has invented it"?﴾ That is, "Muhammad has fabricated it." Here "am" (أَمْ) is the munqati'ah (disjunctive) particle, meaning "bal" (rather) together with the hamzah of interrogation. Its meaning is: "Rather, do they say, 'He has invented it'?!" This is a rejection of their saying and an expression of wonder at them, because his matter is manifest in that their eloquent ones were unable to produce the like of three verses from it.

﴿Rather, it is the truth﴾, then he turned from rejection to affirming that it is the truth,

﴿from your Lord﴾, and Muhammad (ﷺ) did not invent it as they claimed, out of obstinacy and ignorance.

﴿That you may warn a people﴾, that is, the Arabs,

﴿to whom no warner has come before you﴾. "Ma" (مَا) here is for negation, and the clause is a description (sifah) of "qawman" (a people).

﴿That they may perhaps be guided﴾. This "perhaps" (لَعَلَّ) expresses tarajji (hope) on the part of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), just as in "perhaps he may be reminded" (لَعَلَّهُ يَتَذَكَّرُ) it expresses hope on the part of Moses and Aaron.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 4:

﴿Allah is He who created the heavens and the earth and whatever is between them in six days; then He settled upon the Throne﴾: He took control of it (istawla) by bringing it into being (ihdathihi),

﴿you have not, besides Him,﴾: besides Allah,

﴿any protector or intercessor﴾: meaning, if you transgress His pleasure, you will not find for yourselves any protector (waliyy), i.e., a helper who will support you, nor any intercessor (shafi') who will intercede for you.

﴿Will you not then be mindful?﴾: will you not be admonished by the admonitions of Allah.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 32, verse 5:

﴿He arranges the affair﴾, i.e., the affair of the worldly life,

﴿from the heaven to the earth﴾, until the Hour arises,

﴿then it ascends to Him﴾, all of that affair, i.e., it goes up to Him so that He may judge concerning it,

﴿in a day whose measure is a thousand years﴾, and it is the Day of Resurrection,

﴿of what you count﴾, of the days of the worldly life. There is no support for the *Mushabbiha* (the anthropomorphists) in His saying "ilayhi" ("to Him") for establishing a direction, because its meaning is "to where He is pleased with," or "His command." Likewise, they have no grounds in His saying: ﴿Indeed, I am going to my Lord﴾ [al-Saffat: 99], ﴿Indeed, I am migrating to my Lord﴾ [al-Ankabut: 26], ﴿And whoever leaves his home emigrating to Allah﴾ [al-Nisa: 100].

That is (the One) described as above: Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, ﴿the Almighty﴾, whose command prevails, ﴿the Most Merciful﴾, whose kindness and facilitation are far-reaching. It has been said: there is no pause upon it, because—

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 7:

﴿Who﴾ is its attribute (ṣifah),

﴿made excellent everything He created﴾; i.e., He made it good (ḥassanahu), because everything is arranged according to what wisdom (ḥikmah) requires.

﴿He created it﴾: Kūfī (the Kufan reciters), Nāfi' and Sahl read it as an attribute, meaning: "Everything He created, He made its creation excellent." Others read it as an apposition (badal), meaning: "He made excellent the creation of everything."

﴿And He began the creation of man﴾, i.e., Adam,

﴿from clay﴾.

Then He made his progeny (nasl) from an extract (sulalah), i.e., his descendants (dhurriyyatahu), from a drop (nutfah) of

Wait, let me translate it properly, as the passage is short and must be rendered in full.

Then He made his progeny (nasl), that is, his descendants (dhurriyyah), from an extract (sulalah), that is, from a drop (nutfah) of water (ma'), that is, semen (maniyy), which is a substitute (badal) for "sulalah," (from) a despicable (maheen), weak, insignificant (haqir) (fluid).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 9:

﴿Then He fashioned him﴾, (sawwāhu) made him proportionate (qawwamahu), like His saying: ﴿in the best of stature﴾ [al-Tin: 4]. ﴿And breathed into him﴾, (nafakha) caused to enter (adkhala),

﴿of His spirit﴾, the idafah (genitive construction) here indicates specialization (li-l-ikhtisas), as if He had said: "and breathed into him of the thing that He Himself is specially characterized by, and of His knowledge,"

﴿And made for you hearing and sight and hearts﴾, so that you might hear, see, and understand,

﴿little are you thankful﴾, i.e., you give thanks but little.

"And they say," the speaker being Ubayy ibn Khalaf, and it is attributed to them (the disbelievers in general) because they approved of his saying it.

﴿"When we have strayed into the earth?"﴾ That is: when we have become dust, and gone off mingled with the dust of the earth, not distinguishable from it, as water strays into milk; or we have been hidden in the earth through burial in it. ʿAlī read "ḍalilnā" with a kasra on the lām. It is said: "ḍalla, yaḍillu" and "ḍalla, yaḍallu." The adverbial phrase of time in "a-idhā ḍalalnā" (when we have strayed) is governed by what is indicated by ﴿"Shall we indeed be in a new creation?"﴾, namely "we will be raised."

﴿"Nay, but they are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord."﴾ That is, they deny it. When He mentioned their disbelief in the resurrection, He turned from it to what is more emphatic, namely that they disbelieve in everything that will occur in the end, not in the resurrection alone.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 11:

﴿Say: The angel of death who has been entrusted with you will cause you to die; then to your Lord you will be returned.﴾ That is: the angel of death, who has been entrusted with seizing your souls, will take your souls, and after that you will be returned to your Lord, raised up for reckoning and recompense. This is the meaning of "meeting Allah." And "al-tawaffi" (causing to die, taking in full): the taking of the self, which is the rūḥ (spirit), that is, he seizes your souls entirely, from your saying, "I took my right from so-and-so in full" (tawaffaytu ḥaqqī min fulānin), when you receive it complete and whole, without any deficiency. And on the authority of Mujāhid: "The earth was gathered together for the angel of death, and made for him like a basin (ṭast), from which he takes whatever he wishes." It was also said: the angel of death calls the souls and they answer him, then he orders his assistants to seize them, and Allah (exalted is He) is the One who commands all of that, and He is the Creator of the acts of created beings. This is the way of reconciling this verse with His saying: ﴿Our messengers take him in death﴾ [al-An'am: 61], and His saying: ﴿Allah takes the souls at the time of their death﴾ [al-Zumar: 42].

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 12:

﴿If you could see﴾: the address is to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), or to everyone. The "law" (law) here is imtina'iyya (indicating that the condition is impossible because its consequent is not realized), and its answer is omitted, meaning: "you would see a terrible matter."

﴿when the criminals﴾: they are those who said: "When we have gone astray in the earth..." Both "law" and "idh" (when) are for the past tense. This is permissible because what is awaited from Allah is treated as if it already exists. Nothing that "see" would govern is supposed for "ترى" (tara, "you see"); it is as if it were said: "if the seeing were to be from you." And "idh" is an adverbial clause of time governed by it.

﴿with their heads bowed﴾: from humiliation, shame, and remorse.

﴿before their Lord﴾: before the reckoning of their Lord. It is permissible to pause upon this word, because of the requirement of the omission, since the estimate is: they say: ﴿Our Lord, we have seen and heard﴾, "You have spoken truly in Your promise and Your threat, and we have heard from You the confirmation of Your messengers," or: "We were blind and deaf, but now we see and hear."

﴿So send us back﴾: to the world,

﴿and we will act righteously﴾, that is, faith and obedience,

﴿for indeed we are now certain﴾ of the resurrection and the reckoning.

﴿And had We willed, We would have given every soul its guidance﴾, in this world. That is: had We willed, We would have given every soul what We possess of *lutf* (divine grace, a favour that leads to guidance), which, if they had chosen it, would have guided them. But We did not give them that *lutf*, because We knew that they would choose disbelief and prefer it. This is an argument against the Mu'tazilah (the rationalist school of theology), for they hold that God willed to give every soul that by which it would be guided, and He has given it, but it did not become guided. They interpreted the verse as referring to the will of compulsion (*jabr*), and this interpretation is corrupt, as is known in *Tabsirat al-Adilla* (a work of kalam by al-Nasafi's contemporary scholars).

﴿But the word from Me has come into effect: I will surely fill Hell with jinn and humankind, all together﴾. But the word from Me became binding, with what I knew would proceed from them, that which would merit Hell for them. This is what He knew of them, that they would choose rejection and denial. In singling out humankind and jinn there is an indication that He preserved His angels from any deed that would merit Hell for them.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 15:

﴿Only those believe in Our signs who, when they are reminded of them, fall down prostrating﴾, i.e., who are admonished by them,

﴿and glorify the praise of their Lord﴾, they prostrate to Allah out of humility, submission, and gratitude for what He has granted them of Islam,

﴿and glorify the praise of their Lord﴾, they declare Allah free of whatever is unbefitting to Him, and they praise Him, extolling Him,

﴿and they are not arrogant﴾, against believing in Him and prostrating to Him.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 16:

﴿Tatajafa﴾ (they withdraw, are lifted away): tartafiʿu (they rise), and tatanahha (they move aside),

﴿junūbuhum ʿani l-maḍājiʿi﴾ (their sides from the beds): ʿan al-furush (from the bedding), and maḍājiʿ al-nawm (the places of sleep). Sahl said: He bestowed a gift upon a people, which is that He permitted them to converse with Him intimately, and made them among the people of His intimacy, then He praised them for it, saying: ﴿Their sides withdraw from the beds, calling﴾, calling out,

﴿upon their Lord﴾, worshipping Him,

﴿in fear and in hope﴾: an object of purpose (maf'ūl lahu), meaning: "out of fear of His displeasure and hope for His mercy." They are those who perform tahajjud (voluntary night prayer). It is related from the Prophet (ﷺ) concerning its explanation: "The servant standing in prayer during the night." It is related from Ibn ʿAtaʾ: "Their sides refused to rest on the carpet of heedlessness, and sought the carpet of nearness," meaning the night prayer. It is related from Anas: Some of the Companions of the Prophet (ﷺ) would pray from the Maghrib prayer until the last ʿIshāʾ prayer, and this verse was revealed concerning them. It was also said: They are those who pray the ʿatamah prayer (ʿIshāʾ) and do not sleep through it.

﴿And from what We have provided them, they spend﴾, in obedience to Allah (Exalted).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (*Madarik al-Tanzil*) on surah 32, verse 17:

﴿فَلا تَعْلَمُ نَفْسٌ ما أُخْفِيَ لَهُمْ﴾ "Fa-la ta'lamu nafsun ma ukhfiya lahum" ("So no soul knows what has been hidden for them"). "Ma" is in the sense of "alladhi" (the relative pronoun "that which"). "Ukhfiya" (the verb "has been hidden") is in the form that reports the words of the soul, according to Hamzah and Ya'qub (two of the canonical readers, *qurra'*).

﴿مِن قُرَّةِ أعْيُنٍ﴾ "min qurrati a'yun" ("of comfort for the eyes"). That is, no one knows what honour has been prepared for these people.

﴿جَزاءً﴾ "jaza'an" ("as a reward") is a verbal noun (*masdar*), meaning: they are recompensed with a reward.

﴿بِما كانُوا يَعْمَلُونَ﴾ "bima kanu ya'malun" ("for what they used to do"). From al-Hasan, may Allah have mercy on him: "The people concealed their deeds in the world, so Allah concealed for them what no eye has seen and no ear has heard." In this there is evidence that what is meant is the prayer in the depths of the night, so that the reward corresponds to the deed.

Then he explained that whoever is in the light of obedience and faith is not equal to whoever is in the darkness of disbelief and disobedience, by His saying: ﴿Is one who is a believer like one who is a defiant sinner?﴾ That is: a disbeliever. Both [phrases] are construed according to the wording of "man" (who), and His saying ﴿they are not equal﴾ is construed according to the meaning, as evidenced by His saying:

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 19:

﴿As for those who believe and do righteous deeds, for them are the Gardens of Refuge (jannat al-ma'wa) as an abode﴾, it is a kind of gardens, where the spirits of the martyrs take refuge. And it was said: it is to the right of the Throne.

﴿As a welcoming gift (nuzulan) for what they used to do﴾, a reward for their deeds. And "al-nuzul" (the welcoming gift): the provision given to the guest who arrives, then it became general.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 20:

﴿As for those who defied (fasaqu), their refuge is the Fire﴾: that is, their shelter (malja'uhum) and their dwelling-place.

﴿Every time they wish to come out of it, they will be returned into it, and it will be said to them﴾: that is, the keepers of the Fire (khazanat al-nar) will say to them: ﴿Taste the punishment of the Fire which you used to deny﴾. This is evidence that what is meant by the defiant (al-fasiq) is the disbeliever (al-kafir), since denial (al-takdhib) is the opposite of faith (al-iman).

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 21:

﴿And We will surely make them taste the lesser punishment﴾, i.e., the punishment of this world: captivity, and the afflictions they suffered from the years of famine, seven years,

﴿short of the greater punishment﴾, i.e., the punishment of the Hereafter. That is: We will make them taste the punishment of this world before they reach the Hereafter. From al-Darani (al-Darani): "The lesser punishment is abandonment (al-khudhlan, being forsaken by God), and the greater punishment is eternal abiding in the fires." It was also said: the lesser punishment is the punishment of the grave ('adhab al-qabr),

﴿so that they may﴾, that is, so that those punished with the lesser punishment ﴿return﴾, i.e., repent of disbelief.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 22:

﴿And who is more unjust than one who is reminded﴾, an admonition, ﴿of the signs of his Lord﴾, i.e., of the Qur'an,

﴿then turns away from them﴾, i.e., turns his back on them and does not reflect upon them. The "then" (thumma) here indicates astonishment (istib'ad), meaning: turning away from such signs, in their clarity, their brightness, and their guidance to the right path and to the attainment of the supreme happiness, after being reminded of them, is far-fetched according to reason. It is like when you say to your companion: "You found an opportunity like that, then you did not seize it?!", expressing astonishment at his failure to seize it.

﴿Indeed, We will take retribution upon the criminals﴾. He did not say "from him," because when He made him the most unjust of every unjust person and then threatened the criminals in general with retribution, this indicates that the most unjust receives the largest share of retribution. Had He said it with a pronoun, this benefit would not have been conveyed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 23:

﴿And We certainly gave Moses the Book﴾, that is, the Torah,

﴿So do not be in doubt﴾, that is, in suspicion,

﴿about meeting him﴾, that is, about meeting Moses, the Book; or about your meeting Moses on the night of the Mi'raj (the Night Ascent); or on the Day of Resurrection; or about Moses meeting his Lord in the Hereafter. Thus it is related from the Prophet (ﷺ).

﴿And We made it a guidance for the Children of Israel﴾, and We made the Book revealed to Moses a guidance for his people.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 24:

﴿And We made from among them leaders﴾, with two hamzas, [read so by] Kufan and Shami [readers],

﴿guiding﴾ people by that, and calling them to what is in the Torah of the religion of Allah and His laws,

﴿by Our command﴾, i.e., commanding them to that,

﴿when they were patient﴾, at the time they were patient in obeying Allah in upholding the truth, or in refraining from sins. [The reading] "lamma sabaru" [with lam and tashdid, i.e., "because they were patient"] is [read so by] Hamza and Ali, meaning: because of their patience in [giving up] the world. This indicates that the fruit of patience is leadership of the people,

﴿and they were certain of Our signs﴾, i.e., the Torah,

﴿with certainty﴾, that is, they knew with a knowledge in which no doubt mingles.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 25:

﴿Indeed, your Lord — He is the one who will decide﴾, that is, He will judge,

﴿between them on the Day of Resurrection﴾, between the prophets and their nations, or between the believers and the polytheists,

﴿concerning that about which they used to differ﴾, so that the truthful is made manifest from the falsifier.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 26:

﴿Awa-lam﴾: the wa (و) here is a conjunction (ʿatf) coordinating with an implied preceding element of the same kind as what follows, i.e., "Awa-lam yadʿu" ("Did they not call [to mind]...?").

﴿yahdi﴾: it means "yubayyin" (makes clear). The subject (fāʿil) is Allah, as shown by the reading of Zayd on the authority of Yaʿqub: "nahdi" (with the first person plural, "We make clear").

﴿lahum﴾: for the people of Makkah.

Kam (كَمْ): it is not permissible for kam to be the subject (fāʿil) of yahdi, because kam is an interrogative (istifhām), and what precedes it cannot govern it. Its position is in the accusative (naṣb) by His saying: ﴿We destroyed before them many generations﴾, such as ʿAd, Thamud, and the people of Lut.

﴿they walk in their dwellings﴾: that is, the people of Makkah pass by their ruins in their own dwellings and lands.

﴿Indeed in that are signs. Will they not hear?﴾: that is, the admonitions, so that they would take heed.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 27:

﴿Do they not see that We drive the water﴾, i.e., We bring the rain and the rivers,

﴿to the barren land﴾, meaning the land whose vegetation has been cut off (jaraza), i.e., cut off, either for lack of water or because it has been grazed. It is not said of land that does not produce plants, such as salt-flats (sibakh), that it is "juruz," according to His saying: ﴿So We bring forth thereby﴾, by the water,

﴿crops from which their livestock eat﴾, from the crops,

﴿and themselves﴾, from their grain (habb), and their livestock from their fodder (ʿasf),

﴿Will they not then see?﴾, with their eyes, so that they might infer from it His power to bring the dead back to life?!

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 28:

﴿And they say, "When is this victory?"﴾ Al-Nasr (victory), or al-fasl (the decisive judgment) bi'l-hukumah (by ruling), from His saying: "Our Lord, judge between us and our people with truth" [7:89]. The Muslims used to say: "Indeed, Allah will grant us victory over the polytheists, or will judge between us and them." When the polytheists heard that, they said: "When is this victory?" That is: at what time will it occur? ﴿If you are truthful﴾, in that it will come to pass.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 29:

﴿Say: "On the Day of Victory"﴾ That is: the Day of Resurrection, which is the Day of Decision between the believers and their enemies. Or "the day of their victory over them," or "the Day of Badr," or "the Day of the Conquest of Makkah."

﴿The faith of those who disbelieve will not benefit them, nor will they be reprieved.﴾ This statement does not, outwardly, correspond to their question as an answer. However, since their purpose in asking about the time of the Victory was to hasten it, in a manner of denial and mockery, they were answered according to what was known of their purpose in their question. So it was said to them: "Do not hasten it, and do not mock." It is as if I see you when you have reached that day and have believed, but faith will not benefit you; or you have sought a respite in order to escape the punishment, but you will not be given respite. As for one who interpreted it as "the Day of the Conquest" or "the Day of Badr," he means those among them who would be killed, for their faith will not benefit them at the moment of being killed, just as the faith of Pharaoh did not benefit him at the time of drowning.

Commentary of al-Nasafi (Madarik al-Tanzil) on surah 32, verse 30:

﴿So turn away from them and wait,﴾ for the victory over them and their destruction.

﴿Indeed, they too are waiting,﴾ for the triumph over you and your destruction. «The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would not sleep until he recited "Alif-Lam-Mim, the Revelation" (al-Sajdah), and "Blessed is He in whose hand is the Dominion" (al-Mulk).» And he said: «Whoever recites "Alif-Lam-Mim, the Revelation" in his house, Satan will not enter it for three days.» And on the authority of Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him), he said: "The surah "Alif-Lam-Mim, the Revelation" is the one that prevents; it protects from the punishment of the grave."
